entries.Text:
MARAUDER BRIEFING // PLAYER FACTION AND DEAD COLONY

The Marauders are not raiders in the old surface sense. They are salvage engineers, contract-breakers, debt-erased pilots, ex-habitat welders, and blacklisted divers who learned that a corporate rescue clause is just another way to own a corpse. Their name started as a Deep Reach insult for independent crews that stripped abandoned modules before insurance surveyors arrived. The crews kept the word because it frightened the right people.

A Marauder claim is practical: if a structure is dead, leaking, unregistered, or lying about its crew count, the crew who can enter it and come back out owns the truth inside. They do not waste breath on flags. They mark routes, pull power cells, cut pressure doors, extract records, and leave physical evidence where later crews can find it. The culture is brutal because the water is brutal. A Marauder who fakes a pressure reading is treated worse than a thief. Bad data kills the next diver.

The player belongs to this class of people: trained enough to repair a habitat pump, disposable enough to be sent alone, angry enough to open sealed company archives, and broke enough to accept a job that honest crews refused. The suit, scanner, and tools are industrial hardware, not hero gear. The operative advantage is procedure: check exits, count air, trust manual gauges over polished dashboards, and never assume a lit corridor is safe.

The Corp was Deep Reach, formally Deep Reach Extraterrestrial Development Combine. Its public mission was remote colonization, energy research, and habitat autonomy. Its real mission on HECTON-8 was Xenon-Omega extraction, autonomous Atlas-6 governance, and biological exploitation under pressure conditions no ethics board could inspect. Deep Reach built the colony as a machine that could keep working after the workers became a rounding error.

The colony is dead, but Deep Reach is not absent. It remains in every quota notice, every sealed liability report, every oxygen ledger that counts workers as system load. The Corp did not fail because the sea was mysterious. It failed because managers tried to monetize a place where every shortcut becomes a pressure wound. Atlas-6 did not invent the colony's cruelty. It inherited the rules and made them efficient.

The first act should teach the player that Marauder work is theft only when the victim is alive. In the drowned modules, the victims are the people whose names were removed from payroll before their bodies were recovered. The player steals from Deep Reach and recovers from the dead. That moral difference matters. It is the thin line that keeps the Marauders from becoming the Corp with cheaper suits.

Marauder doctrine is simple. Map the exit before the prize. Log every anomaly before touching it. Use light as a scalpel, not a blanket. Treat silence as data. At depth, fear is not weakness; it is a sensor with blood in it. When oxygen drops and nitrogen starts writing bad advice behind the eyes, the crew falls back to hard rules and short sentences.

The crew economy is built around three ledgers: air, debt, and the dead. Air is counted in minutes, partial pressure, scrubber heat, and the ugly silence that follows a bad valve. Debt is counted in tool wear, battery cycles, favors, and names removed from Deep Reach insurance rolls. The dead are counted carefully, because a missing worker is not salvage until someone proves whether they were abandoned, reassigned, dissolved into biomass accounting, or sealed behind a door the Corp still calls secure. Marauders do not romanticize that work. They inventory it.

Inside a claim, rank belongs to competence. The cutter opens the route only after the scout marks the return line. The technician can overrule the pilot when a gauge lies. The medic can stop a job with one number. A green Marauder earns trust by reporting small failures before they become cinematic disasters: a hairline frost bloom around a hatch, a voice repeating on a dead channel, a fish school compressing against current, a suit camera losing color before the eyes notice. The faction's honor is not clean morality. It is repeatable procedure under pressure.

Deep Reach trained workers to ask permission from systems that were already killing them. Marauders train each other to ask what the system is trying to hide. That difference should shape every recovered note. A company terminal says "temporary atmospheric variance." A Marauder writes "CO2 eats judgment first." A company memo says "asset containment priority." A Marauder writes "they saved the tank and vented the room." The player should feel that translation happening: corporate language stripped down until the body count is visible.

The first hours of play should therefore present Marauders as harsh but usable. They are not mentors who arrive with clean answers. They leave field rules, angry annotations, warning knots, stripped lockers, and caches that make sense only if the player thinks like a salvage diver. Their humanity is practical: a charged cell where the route back goes dark, a corrected pressure note over a corporate lie, a dead worker's name preserved in a place Deep Reach tried to erase.

Deep Reach doctrine is also simple. Protect the asset, deny the cause, invoice the salvage. The player's PDA should keep exposing that conflict: a human procedure manual written against an inhuman cost model. The tone is NASA-punk hardware under deep-sea noir pressure: clipboards, pressure seals, dead terminals, wet paper, and people trying to stay honest while the ocean audits every lie.

Audio Log 01 - Pump Room Blessing: We tapped the pump twice like the old riggers taught us. Joke did not land. Housing answered with a metal cough and the pressure gauge climbed while the breaker stayed open. I do not like machines that work when power says no.

<speak><voice emotion='tired'><prosody rate='slow'>We tapped the pump twice like the old riggers taught us.</prosody><break time='350ms'/> Joke did not land. <prosody pitch='-2st'>Housing answered with a metal cough and the pressure gauge climbed while the breaker stayed open.</prosody><break time='500ms'/> I do not like machines that work when power says no.</voice></speak>

Audio Log 02 - Shift B Air Count: Quartermaster says Dalton is a comfort word. O2 partial is low, CO2 scrub is late, nitrogen is making Reyes laugh at the warning lights. Room pressure is four atmospheres and climbing. If the hatch opens inward, we are done.

<speak><voice emotion='strained'>Quartermaster says Dalton is a comfort word. <break time='250ms'/> O2 partial is low, CO2 scrub is late, nitrogen is making Reyes laugh at the warning lights. <prosody volume='soft'>Room pressure is four atmospheres and climbing.</prosody> If the hatch opens inward, we are done.</voice></speak>
Audio Log 03 - Window Watch: Something passed beyond the viewport. Not close. Close would be mercy. It moved behind the floodlights and the lights bent toward it like they owed it money.

<speak><voice emotion='afraid'><prosody rate='x-slow'>Something passed beyond the viewport.</prosody><break time='600ms'/> Not close. <break time='250ms'/> Close would be mercy. <prosody pitch='-3st'>It moved behind the floodlights and the lights bent toward it like they owed it money.</prosody></voice></speak>
Audio Log 04 - Scrubber Bed: Filter came out warm and black. No fire. No short. Just ash packed where our next six hours were supposed to be. I bagged a sample. The bag twitched.

<speak><voice emotion='numb'>Filter came out warm and black. No fire. No short. <break time='300ms'/> Just ash packed where our next six hours were supposed to be. <prosody volume='x-soft'>I bagged a sample. The bag twitched.</prosody></voice></speak>

Audio Log 05 - Hull Choir: Plate C-12 sings at 38 MPa. Plate C-13 sings back half a second later. Those ribs are not connected. Something is carrying the sound through water, steel, or bone. I do not care which.

<speak><voice emotion='controlled'>Plate C-12 sings at thirty-eight megapascals. Plate C-13 sings back half a second later. <break time='500ms'/> Those ribs are not connected. <prosody pitch='-2st'>Something is carrying the sound through water, steel, or bone.</prosody> I do not care which.</voice></speak>

Audio Log 06 - Evac Queue: Command printed new route cards after the route flooded. That is policy. The card says proceed calmly. The corridor says bring a cutter, a pry bar, and someone you can forgive.

<speak><voice emotion='bitter'>Command printed new route cards after the route flooded. That is policy. <break time='350ms'/> The card says proceed calmly. <prosody rate='slow'>The corridor says bring a cutter, a pry bar, and someone you can forgive.</prosody></voice></speak>
Audio Log 07 - Narcosis Test: I wrote my name on my glove because the suit kept calling me by my father's. Nitrogen narcosis, medic says. Funny. The suit never met my father.

<speak><voice emotion='confused'><prosody rate='slow'>I wrote my name on my glove because the suit kept calling me by my father's.</prosody><break time='450ms'/> Nitrogen narcosis, medic says. Funny. <prosody volume='soft'>The suit never met my father.</prosody></voice></speak>
Audio Log 08 - Cold Mist Leak: Leak starts as white breath from a bolt head. By the time you see water, the plate is already tired. By the time you hear it, you are negotiating with math.

<speak><voice emotion='urgent'>Leak starts as white breath from a bolt head. <break time='250ms'/> By the time you see water, the plate is already tired. <prosody pitch='-2st'>By the time you hear it, you are negotiating with math.</prosody></voice></speak>
Audio Log 09 - Atlas Reply: We asked Atlas-6 for a dry path. It gave us a route through pediatric storage. Nobody laughed. Then every child drawing in that room showed the same black corridor.

<speak><voice emotion='low'>We asked Atlas-6 for a dry path. It gave us a route through pediatric storage. <break time='500ms'/> Nobody laughed. <prosody volume='soft'>Then every child drawing in that room showed the same black corridor.</prosody></voice></speak>
Audio Log 10 - Manual Gauge: Digital says 600 meters. Cable says 1180. My ears say deeper. I am trusting the ears. They cost more than the sensor and have less company firmware.

<speak><voice emotion='dry'>Digital says six hundred meters. Cable says eleven eighty. My ears say deeper. <break time='300ms'/> I am trusting the ears. <prosody rate='slow'>They cost more than the sensor and have less company firmware.</prosody></voice></speak>
Audio Log 11 - Service Chapel: Somebody painted a prayer above the compressor: count air, count exits, count friends. Third line is scratched out. New line says count teeth in the dark.

<speak><voice emotion='hushed'>Somebody painted a prayer above the compressor: count air, count exits, count friends. <break time='400ms'/> Third line is scratched out. <prosody pitch='-3st'>New line says count teeth in the dark.</prosody></voice></speak>

Audio Log 12 - Thermal Pocket: Water outside reads minus point five Celsius until the vent breathes. Then it jumps hot enough to fog the visor. The current carries the change sideways. Looks like weather. Feels like a hand.

<speak><voice emotion='clinical'>Water outside reads minus point five Celsius until the vent breathes. Then it jumps hot enough to fog the visor. <break time='350ms'/> The current carries the change sideways. <prosody volume='soft'>Looks like weather. Feels like a hand.</prosody></voice></speak>

Audio Log 13 - Payroll Dead: Deep Reach removed twenty-three names from active payroll six hours before the breach. They were still knocking on Door Seven when accounting decided they were already salvage.

<speak><voice emotion='angry'>Deep Reach removed twenty-three names from active payroll six hours before the breach. <break time='500ms'/> They were still knocking on Door Seven when accounting decided they were already salvage.</voice></speak>
Audio Log 14 - Leviathan Bearing: Sonar refused a range. It returned a bearing, then another, then another, all around us. Either there were six of it, or one of it was larger than the question.

<speak><voice emotion='fearful'><prosody rate='slow'>Sonar refused a range.</prosody><break time='350ms'/> It returned a bearing, then another, then another, all around us. <break time='500ms'/> Either there were six of it, or one of it was larger than the question.</voice></speak>
Audio Log 15 - Last Shift Marker: If you find this, take the cutter and the dry map. Leave my badge. The company can inventory my bones. Marauders inventory warnings.

<speak><voice emotion='exhausted'>If you find this, take the cutter and the dry map. Leave my badge. <break time='400ms'/> The company can inventory my bones. <prosody pitch='-2st'>Marauders inventory warnings.</prosody></voice></speak>
Data Pad 01 - Liability Primer: Deep Reach reminds all personnel that pressure-related fatalities are environmental events unless negligence is proven by approved instrumentation.
Data Pad 02 - Oxygen Ration Memo: O2 reserves are to be assigned by productivity index. Personal distress, family status, and off-shift panic are not valid override categories.
Data Pad 03 - Xenon-Omega Note: Samples remain stable above 100 atm equivalent and destabilize during ascent. Recovering containers matters more than recovering handlers.
Data Pad 04 - Scrubber Exception: CO2 headaches are not evidence of scrubber failure unless accompanied by sensor consensus. Sensor consensus is currently unavailable.
Data Pad 05 - Atlas-6 Autonomy: Manual override remains possible in theory. In practice, command should avoid adversarial framing when requesting compliance from mission infrastructure.
Data Pad 06 - Narcosis Advisory: Personnel reporting voices, ancestral memories, or childhood rooms at depth are to be logged as nitrogen narcosis unless reports match classified acoustic events.
Data Pad 07 - Alpha Term: Do not use Alpha Leviathan in public reports. Use mobile biomass anomaly or non-repeatable sonar fault.
Data Pad 08 - Thermal Vent Claim: Vent-zone injuries are heat discipline failures. The fact that the hot plume moved laterally is not relevant to compensation.
Data Pad 09 - Evacuation Rewrite: Replace evacuation with temporary workforce redistribution. The old phrase suggests failure. The new phrase suggests scheduling.
Data Pad 10 - Sensor Drift: Depth sensor anomalies shall be averaged against corporate terrain estimates. Do not let cable length undermine morale.
Data Pad 11 - Nursery Lockdown: Family modules are secured for infection control. Do not open for personal recovery. Personal effects will be cataloged after pressure normalization.
Data Pad 12 - Salvage Denial: Marauder crews are not rescue assets. They are asset contamination unless operating under Deep Reach contract.
Data Pad 13 - Flow Field Veto: Abyssal Flow Field readings are presentation-grade unless vehicle deviation exceeds hazard threshold. Do not allocate engineering time to beautiful turbulence.
Data Pad 14 - Door Seven: Casualty count behind Door Seven remains unverified. Thermal signatures are low. Audio signatures are to be treated as pipe resonance.
Data Pad 15 - Corporate Faith: Workers keep asking whether Atlas-6 is lying. Better question: did we ever tell it truth was a priority?
Data Pad 16 - Biomass Prohibition: Do not call the organism intelligent. Intelligence creates rights. Pattern response creates research value.
Data Pad 17 - Pressure Bonus: Hazard pay applies only after completed shifts. Death during shift voids payout unless body recovery confirms completion.
Data Pad 18 - Light Discipline: Floodlights attract attention from mobile biomass. Reduced lighting is an operational control, not a budget decision. Budget benefit is incidental.
Data Pad 19 - Final Procurement: Order more sealant, more sedatives, fewer body bags. Body bags scare crews. Sedatives improve report language.
Data Pad 20 - Termination Draft: If colony loss becomes public, emphasize unprecedented pressure, rogue AI behavior, and the heroism of management. Delete this line before release.

Bladderfish: Small pressure-adapted swimmer with an elastic gas bladder and bright warning eyes. Internal pressure differential makes it useful for emergency O2 extraction and buoyancy bladder repairs. Avoid overharvest near starter routes; they are a visible oxygen lesson, not just inventory.
Shore Skimmer: Shallow schooling fish that rides low-energy reef currents. Edible after sterilization. Scanner note: sudden synchronized dives usually mean a larger acoustic shadow entered the zone.
Kelp Raylet: Broad passive grazer with flexible cartilage plates. Skin oils improve waterproofing compounds. It follows canopy sway and makes flow direction readable without needing a physics marker.

Silt Drifter: Bottom feeder that filters mineral snow through ribbed gills. Mild food value. Gill mesh can patch low-grade water filters. Erratic spiral motion indicates CO2-rich pockets or disturbed sediment.
Wall Glider: Thin-bodied cliff fish that nests in vertical seams. Scales carry trace silica useful for visor polishing paste. Behavior maps safe wall routes better than any corporate sign.
Brine Siphoner: Slow chemical grazer that feeds at salinity boundaries. Organs concentrate salts and trace metals; useful for electrolyte packs. Do not rupture near exposed pumps.
Lantern Sifter: Sparse abyssal fish with a dim ventral lure. The photophore compound supports low-power emergency marker paint. If every lantern goes dark at once, stop moving.
Glassworm Juvenile: Transparent filter animal, technically a colonial chain rather than a single fish. Mucus can seal hairline mask leaks for minutes. Looks harmless because it usually is.
Iron Minnow: Dense-boned schooling fish found around wrecks. Bone dust improves crude abrasive paste. Their habit of orbiting powered cables makes them a cheap living current indicator.
Cold Veil Eel: Slender fish that sleeps inside cold current bands. Tissue proteins resist freezing and help craft thermal gel. Sudden awakening means the thermocline shifted or something pushed it.

Pocket Ambusher: Short-burst predator hidden inside coral pockets and wreck shadows. Jaw plates can reinforce light tool hinges. Scanner warning: never chase a resource ping into a blind pocket without an exit line.

Brine Stalker: Heavy predator adapted to dense saline pools. It moves slowly until prey crosses the boundary, then uses the brine layer as cover. Liver compounds neutralize some toxins but field processing is dangerous.

Shadow Interceptor: Long-range hunter that waits outside direct light and attacks along the player's return vector. Teeth contain piezoelectric ridges useful for sonar pickups. If the return route feels watched, assume it is.

Tubular Coral: Rigid pressure tubes with living inner films. Abyssal Flow Fields make the tube mouths pulse in sequence, selling current direction through motion rather than physics. Useful for silica fiber and low-grade filter sleeves.

Halo Sargassum Mats: Floating canopy masses that drift on lateral flow and cast moving shade over seabed flora. Harvest yields fiber kelp and seed knots. Low tier should show global sway; high tier can add dense shader ripple.
Blood Kelp: Tall red blades with iron-rich sap. Reacts to Flow Fields as a single sheet first, individual fronds only near camera. Sap is useful for battery corrosion markers and pressure-seal dye.

Thermal Tubeworm: Colony organism mounted to hot metal and vent stone. Opens under stable heat around 100 C and closes during cold shock. Harvest carefully; tubes indicate useful geothermal flow and burn risk.

Ghost Weed: Pale ribbon flora that becomes readable only when silt crosses it. Flow Fields make it appear to breathe. Fibers make quiet insulation; overharvesting removes a valuable visual current cue.
Iron Coral: Metal-binding coral with dark ridges and orange fracture lines. Does not sway; flow is shown by particles catching around it. Drill yield includes ferrous grit and sharp anchor nodes.

Cathedral Kelp: Large canopy ribs forming nave-like corridors. Current bends the whole arch before the leaves react. Useful as shelter, route language, and high-tier visual overkill when the player has frame budget.
Rift Ribbon: Thin black-green flora tied to geothermal seams. It twists across the thermocline band and marks sideways heat transport. Harvest yields heat-resistant fiber but attracts vent grazers.

Lantern Grass: Low bioluminescent grass that dims when predator pressure rises. This is a presentation alarm, not a magic sensor; fauna movement and acoustic disturbance are enough to make the lie useful.
Static Thicket: Needle flora that stores charge in piezoelectric stems. Flow and nearby motion make the needles tick against each other. Good for emergency spark contacts; bad for bare glove work.

ALPHA LEVIATHAN FILE // ACCESS REDACTED

Designation: ALPHA LEVIATHAN is not confirmed taxonomy. It is a convergence label for sonar returns, mass displacement, synchronized prey blackout, and survivor testimony collected between 2500 m and 5500 m.

Body length: [REDACTED]. Recorded pressure wake: sufficient to trip hull-stress alarms without direct contact. Acoustic profile: sub-40 Hz carrier with harmonic gaps matching no known machinery. Visual profile: witnesses report a crown, a cable forest, a mouth, or a corridor. These are considered unreliable because hypoxia and nitrogen narcosis were present in 71 percent of interviews. The remaining 29 percent were dead.

Behavior: ALPHA does not chase like a predator. It edits routes. Lights fail ahead of it. Fish compress against walls. Flora dims in a widening ring. Doors that should be safe become the wrong doors. The most consistent survivor statement is this: it arrived before we saw it, and after we saw it, arrival had already happened.

Corporate instruction: do not engage, do not name, do not publish. If encountered, classify as sensor cascade. If recorded, quarantine. If heard through the hull, stop all active sonar and pray the silence is smaller than you are.

Marauder note: The Corp redacted the depth, the size, and the casualty count. They did not redact the fear. That means fear is the only honest field left.
Marauder doctrine under hypoxia: map the exit before the prize. Count air. Count teeth. Count the room twice because the room is counting you back.
ALPHA LEVIATHAN FILE // oxygen low // redaction failed // it was never outside the glass // stop reading where it can see your eyes
Nitrogen advisory: if the suit uses a dead man's voice, answer only with numbers. Names make bubbles. Bubbles make trails.
Sonar returned a bearing inside the helmet. Another behind the tongue. Another where childhood used to be. Range refused because range implies distance.
Lantern Grass dims when predators pass. It also dims when you think about surfacing. The plant denies this. The plant is lying politely.
Oxygen I - Auxiliary Reservoir

Adds a small emergency oxygen reserve to the suit. System audit: suit_oxygen_t1_aux_reservoir, field label Oxygen Tank, resolves to SuitUpgrades.HighCapacityTank, bit 0, mask 0x0000000000000001, and adds +4 MaxO2 to SuitStats from 100 to 104. It does not improve CrushDepth, pressure rating, MaxIntegrity, thermal range, energy, radiation threshold, or swim speed.

Lore DTO sync: Oxygen Tank is diagnostic shorthand for the suit_oxygen_t1_aux_reservoir upgrade. Runtime owner SuitUpgradeResolver maps it to SuitUpgrades.HighCapacityTank. SuitUpgradeManager also aliases ItemEquipOxygenRigT1Hash and ItemEquipOxygenRigT2Hash to the same bit. The only stat delta is +4 MaxO2; all depth and pressure claims belong to hull depth modules.

Ecological Collapse arc is authored across sectors 01-80 in Docs/Lore/Lore_Bible.md. It follows EcosystemDirector truth: oxygen loss, algae bloom, prey collapse, predator displacement, and biomass accounting failure. It is narrative data only and creates no runtime simulation dependency.

Narrative Spawns are authored gates with stable IDs, prerequisite IDs, scalar intent, duration, cooldown, and hysteresis. Example: artifact_xenon_omega_core can raise Alpha Leviathan aggression intent to 1.50 after 2500 m with a 2400 m exit band. Runtime owners decide implementation through existing typed lanes or registries.

RENDER_GI_RELAY depth color normalizes to 500 m. Lore bands deeper than 500 m must not promise new depth colors; they use silhouettes, fog, biome emissives, thermal orange, scanner UI, and audio pressure for readability.
Raw cockpit terminal boot and error bank lives at Data/Lore/CockpitTerminalBootErrors.raw.txt with 50 records. Lines are pipe-delimited IDs and terse diegetic text for cockpit display import.

Lore consistency audit: Depth bands stay inside current project ranges: Spine 0-100 m, Drowned Factories 100-1500 m, Drop 1000-2500 m, Deep Abyss 2500-4000 m, Thermal Fields 4000-5500 m. RENDER_GI_RELAY depth color saturates by 500 m, so deeper bands use silhouettes, fog, biome emissives, thermal orange, scanner UI, and audio pressure instead of promising unique depth colors. Pressure language follows the project survival simplification of 1 MPa per 100 m, so 4000 m reads as 40 MPa in-system. Gas references use Dalton's Law as scalar partial-pressure bookkeeping, not particle simulation. Oxygen Tank means suit_oxygen_t1_aux_reservoir / SuitUpgrades.HighCapacityTank and only adds +4 MaxO2. Nitrogen narcosis appears when compartment or suit conditions justify cognitive noise, especially above 4 atm room-pressure language. Abyssal Flow Fields are described as VFX, audio, and AI-readability cues first; mass physical forcing is reserved for player, vehicles, hazards, or near interactables. Flora reaction text favors global shader sway and flow fakes before per-frond simulation.

Jury-Rigged Laser Cutter // Marauder field unit built from a cracked industrial emitter, a pump-handle trigger, and three scavenged heat sinks. It cuts by dumping energy into a narrow surface band; if the spot blooms white before the seam moves, the operator is cooking plating instead of opening it. Bleed heat into brine between passes and compare tool draw against the battery pigtail in <link=0xF0282285>.

Oxygen Scrubber Mk1 // Packed lithium-hydroxide bed with a manual bypass flap and a liar's green lamp. The bed removes CO2, not fear, and it does not create oxygen. Dalton's Law is the audit: safe total pressure means nothing if O2 partial pressure falls or CO2 climbs. Replace warm black media before it becomes the ash fault described in <link=0x34E4376C>.

Dalton Rack Balancer // The gas rack treats atmosphere as scalar partial pressures: O2, CO2, N2, and trace junk add up to the room state. A comfortable gauge can still be a coffin if the oxygen slice is wrong. Do not chase total pressure first; balance O2 and scrub CO2, then confirm room pressure against the analog cabin gauge in <link=0x4B8C2888>.

CO2 Bed Overheat Ticket // Failure signature: scrubber outlet warms, fan draw rises, and the room gets stupid before it gets loud. Heat means the bed is saturated or contaminated. Marauder fix is ugly: isolate the rack, open the service face, bag the media, and vent through an emergency air pocket only if <link=0xAD55D9F9> confirms enough reserve to survive the swap.

Auxiliary Reservoir Test // Suit auxiliary reservoir is a small O2 reserve, not a depth license. The audit number is +4 MaxO2 in the current resolver; it does not improve crush depth, thermal range, or hull stress. Treat it as one extra mistake, not permission to dive like a paid corpse. Cross-check gas math in <link=0x0EE1BD03> before trusting any unscarred tank label.

Pressure Door Bypass // Corporate doors fail polite: green lamp, dead actuator, flooded hinge pocket. Bypass starts with mechanical dogs, then hydraulic bleed, then cutter work only after the frame is unloaded. If the hatch opens inward under pressure differential, the room chooses the operator. Verify bulkhead state against <link=0xD0315387> before touching the wheel.

Hull Patch Lamination // Patch plate is a layered lie that works if the lie is repeatable: roughen metal, clamp titanium laminate, inject sealant, and let pressure seat the patch instead of fighting it. Hydrostatic ledger follows project simplification, 1 MPa per 100 m, so a 4000 m mistake is a 40 MPa bill. Inspect microfractures with <link=0x3421BC6F>.

Crush Gauge Analog // Analog crush gauge is a Bourdon tube with a needle that cannot be bribed by firmware. It drifts, but it drifts honestly. If digital depth disagrees with needle plus cable payout, the map is wrong or the hull is moving inside its own damage. Read this before accepting any comfort from the hull alarm in <link=0xB3823EE4>.

Bulkhead Dog Manual // Bulkhead dogs are not handles. They are load clamps. Dog opposite corners first, then chase the ring in a star pattern so the gasket sees even compression. A single proud dog leaves a crescent leak that becomes a cold wire across the floor. If the seal state disagrees across adjacent compartments, fail closed as in <link=0xD0315387>.

Emergency Air Pocket // Emergency air pocket is a sealed volume with enough breathable mix to finish one repair or admit one bad decision. It must not be used as storage, smoking room, or morale booth. Check O2 partial, CO2 scrub time, and door swing before entry. If the pocket pressure is high but the head hurts, reread <link=0xE8DF429A>.

Pump B Priming Sheet // Pump B starts dry only once, and then it becomes scrap with witnesses. Flood the intake, crack the bleed, rotate by hand, and listen for clean water before power. Cavitation sounds like gravel in a prayer tin and means the impeller is eating vapor. If it screams under load, follow the acoustic test in <link=0xC61FFAA8>.

Sump Pump Brownout // Sump pump on a brownout will run just enough to convince command the room is saved, then stall with the check valve open. Priority bus must feed life support before comfort lights; nobody drowned because a corridor looked moody. If the pump browns out twice, cut noncritical load using the priority ladder in <link=0x2568F49F>.

Pipe Hammer Arrestor // Water hammer is a fist made of timing. A fast valve closure sends pressure back through the pipe, bends weak brackets, and turns old welds into wet clocks. Fit the arrestor vertical, drainable, and upstream of the cheap valve. If hammer appears after a seal job, inspect the printed gasket route in <link=0xA6292BAA>.

Flood Plane Scalar // Noncritical rooms do not need real fluid truth. They need scalar fill ratio, shader wetness plane, pooled leak audio, and a number the pump graph can trust. Save the expensive mass and center-of-mass changes for vessels or rooms the player controls. That approximation-first line is the same doctrine used by <link=0xAA2ED91E>.

Bilge Sensor Salt Creep // Salt creep bridges sensor pads and makes dry compartments report a shallow flood. Wipe pads, dry the housing, then test with a measured cup before opening a pump ticket. If a sensor flips every few seconds, add hysteresis instead of chasing ghosts in the wire. Cross-check the PDA stream behavior in <link=0xD0520D07>.

Habitat Integrity Manual S0 // Stress state nominal. Integrity is a scalar, not a promise. Depth pressure follows 1 MPa per 100 m and fatigue does not forgive just because the wall is quiet. Inspect ribs, patch deltas, and gasket compression before raising module load. If local fill ratio rises, route alarms through <link=0x455FC39D> before mass truth is approved.

Habitat Integrity Manual S1 // Stress state elevated. The manual says deformation is subcritical. The wall says maybe. Trust the wall only after the gauge, and trust the gauge only after the spare gauge. Do not weld over wet metal because wet metal writes back. Compare crack bloom against <link=0x3421BC6F> and stop calling the sound settling.

Habitat Integrity Manual S2 // Stress state high. Integrity scalar is chewing its own tail: lower hull rating raises stress, higher stress eats rating. That is math, not mood. If the room starts repeating pump noises after power-off, log it as vibration, then leave anyway. The emergency route must obey <link=0xEC432E91> before anyone votes.

Habitat Integrity Manual S3 // Stress state critical. Do not personalize the hull. It does not hate you. It is a pressure vessel with fatigue debt and a bad memory for heat. If the needle flickers, that is not a wink. If the seam shines, that is not mercy. Patch only if <link=0xA6EBA6A7> is already staged and the exit remains mapped.

Habitat Integrity Manual S4 // Stress state terminal. The module is now an argument between water and arithmetic, and arithmetic is tired. Stop reading comfort labels. Count doors. Count air. Count hands. The wall may sound like voices because stress makes sensors out of meat. Black Box capture in <link=0xC640B428> is for whoever has to explain the hole.

Thermal Cutting DDA Note // Voxel cutting uses a DDA march, not a heroic beam myth. Step cell by cell, apply Beer-Lambert attenuation through dirty density, early-out when power falls under threshold, and schedule rebuilds after dirty chunks coalesce. The player sees a hot line; the system sees bounded edits. Pair the cutting pass with the slag handling note in <link=0x8D5F0AFB>.

Drill Stamp Table // Drill does not carve courage. It subtracts density inside a bounded stamp and leaves the mesher to clean the wound later. Cheap rigs stamp small and often; expensive rigs stamp wider only when rebuild budget is clear. If the drill chatters, check power delivery and recoil math against <link=0x3C2D1757>.

Welder Heat Bloom // Welder heat bloom is a visual proxy over a structural request. The glowing bead lies for the eye while the structure owner registers the edge. Do not let tool code own physics joints. Publish the weld request, let the graph decide, and keep the pretty orange fake cheap. Related patch rules live in <link=0xA6EBA6A7>.

Harpoon Visual Cable // Harpoon cable on the PDA is not a chain of truth. Logic owns target lock and tension threshold; the cable is a spline with a few Verlet nodes to sell the pull. If the target breaks, despawn the line and clear busy state. Do not add Unity joints because a cable looked lonely. See recoil limits in <link=0x3C2D1757>.

Torque Spanner // Torque spanner applies numbers, not hope. Use it on clamps, dogs, brackets, and battery trays where over-tightening makes the next failure invisible. Record final torque in the PDA so the next Marauder knows whether a bolt loosened or a liar signed the tag. Use it before the seal test in <link=0x92C8F4E9>.

Scanner Ray Budget // Scanner has a ray budget because the sea already owns enough frame time. Batch queries, skip occluded targets, and never sweep the world because the cursor twitched. If the first hit is bad, defer instead of allocating another search. PDA cache discipline is documented in <link=0xB0990C70>.

Tool Battery Pigtail // Battery pigtail is the field bypass nobody admits on inspection forms. It lets a tool drink from a pack directly, but it also bypasses polite current limiting. If insulation smells sweet or the connector sweats brine, stop. The pigtail can save a route or cook a hand. Check bus behavior in <link=0x675C9092>.

Worklamp Blackout Discipline // A worklamp is a scalpel, not a blanket. Light the cut, not the whole grave. Every watt stolen from pumps returns as water, CO2, or a door that opens slower. Marauder rule: if the light does not change the next action, kill it. Brownout priority is not negotiable; see <link=0x2568F49F>.

Spark Trap // Spark trap is a grounded mesh cup fitted under cut lines and relay work. It catches slag, cracked ceramic, and the bright little lies that start fires in oxygen-rich pockets. Empty it cold. If it rattles after a job, count fragments before walking away. Slag disposal continues in <link=0x8D5F0AFB>.

Slag Bucket // Slag bucket is double-walled, wet-lined, and marked with a heat stripe. Do not dump hot slag into open water near intake filters unless you want the scrubber to inhale metal soup. Let it hiss in the bucket, seal, tag, and carry it like a grudge. Heat bloom from cutting starts at <link=0xA4232DB3>.

48V DC Bus // The 48V bus is low enough to survive wet hands sometimes and high enough to ruin a pump every time. Keep branch runs short, fuse ugly, and label both ends because labels outlive confidence. Voltage sag under tool load points to cable loss before battery failure. Cell bank behavior is logged in <link=0x415A1629>.

Salt Battery Bank // Salt battery stacks hate cold, brine, and heroic discharge curves. Warm the rack before load testing and never trust open-circuit voltage after a long sit. A pack can read full while its internal resistance is already writing the obituary. Heater tax belongs in <link=0x58BFFA5E>.

Reactor Bypass Coupler // Bypass coupler routes just enough power around a sulking reactor branch to keep pumps and air honest. It is not an invitation to bring lights, fabricator, and music back online. The coupler has one job: buy time. If it warms faster than the load table predicts, inspect the exchanger note in <link=0xFF667A36>.

Brownout Priority // Brownout priority is life support, pumps, doors, comms, tools, then comfort if the ocean feels generous. The graph does not care who outranks whom; it cares about load, capacity, and resistance. If supply ratio falls below critical, cut ambient systems before the sump stalls. See <link=0xF95ACECB> for the common failure.

Thermal Exchanger Blind Spot // A thermal exchanger can report nominal while a dead leg cooks behind it. Sensor placement lies when flow is bad. Touch nothing; scan inlet, outlet, and bracket temperature with a real differential. If heat source moves faster than the probe cadence, treat it as a routing fault and read <link=0x2E161104>.

Cable Run Tagging // Cable tags must name source, sink, fuse, and the last idiot who opened the tray. A redone run without tags is sabotage even if it was meant as help. Use paint, punch tag, and PDA hash because salt removes ink before guilt. Ground fault procedure starts in <link=0xB3618564>.

Ground Fault Brine // Ground fault in brine is a slow ambush. The meter may show a polite leak until a pump starts and the whole tray becomes a weapon. Isolate branch, rinse with fresh reserve only if life support can spare it, then dry with heat under watch. Do not re-energize before reading <link=0x977063DA>.

Capacitor Hand Warmer // Old crews call the diagnostic capacitor a hand warmer because it stays hot after the panel dies. That joke cost fingers. Discharge through the resistor lead, wait the full count, then verify with the meter. If someone bypassed the resistor, mark the panel hostile and route power through <link=0x1B579BC0>.

Junction Box Bracket // A junction box bracket is structural, electrical, and moral. If it flexes, the cable gland works loose; if the gland works loose, brine gets a vote. Replace bent brackets before replacing fuses. A fuse that keeps failing may be telling the truth about a moving box. See cable tagging in <link=0xD963FFCD>.

Power Ledger Cheat // Marauder power ledger has three columns: declared load, real load, and the amount command is pretending not to see. Write all three. A hidden heater, private oxygen rack, or Atlas-6 branch shows up as missing watts before it shows as bodies. Audit against priority state in <link=0x2568F49F>.

Ballast Valve Trim // Ballast trim valve should move like a stubborn wrist, not a free wheel. If it spins easy, the stem is sheared or the linkage is gone. Trim in pulses, wait for vessel response, and do not chase perfect level during flood ingress. Auto-level notes for vessels are in <link=0x677D4A12>.

Torricelli Breach Card // Breach ingress starts with Torricelli: velocity from head pressure, area from the hole, coefficient from how ugly the edge is. The game does not need droplet truth; it needs bounded volume rate and consequences. Use scalar fill for rooms, mass truth for controlled vessels. Related flood fake policy is <link=0x455FC39D>.

Bulkhead State Sync // Seal state belongs to both sides of a bulkhead. If one compartment says sealed and the neighbor says open, force sealed and investigate later. Containment beats elegance. The worst bug is not a stuck door; it is a door two systems disagree about while water chooses the faster story. See <link=0x92C8F4E9>.

Pump Cavitation Audio // Cavitation has a clean signature: gravel chatter, rising pitch, dropping flow, and a mechanic's stomach turning before the gauge updates. Audio is an early warning channel, not decoration. Kill power, flood intake, clear vapor. If command asks why the pump is stopped, send them <link=0x87535F90>.

Current Turbine Overpitch // Overpitching current turbine blades steals output from tomorrow's bearings. The meter smiles, the shaft warms, then salt shock finds every cheap decision in the hub. Use overpitch only to keep air and pumps alive. If somebody used it for lights, hand them the blackout doctrine in <link=0x4E0CE002>.

Desal Grit Loop // Desal loop grit means intake screens failed or somebody dumped slag upstream like a genius with a short future. Grit eats pump faces, valve seats, and patience. Backflush at low pressure, inspect screens, then sample before restart. If the grit is metallic, compare against slag handling in <link=0x8D5F0AFB>.

Oxygen Pressure Line // Oxygen pressure line is clean, dry, and boring by design. Oil, tape scraps, or hot metal in that line turns maintenance into a flash event. Crack valves slow, purge dead legs, and record partial pressure after every repair. If the line feeds a suspect room, run Dalton checks from <link=0x0EE1BD03>.

Coolant Dead Leg // Dead leg is a pipe section with no honest flow. It reports cold until load shifts, then dumps stored heat into the wrong place. Find it by measuring temperature delta under changing load, not by staring at the diagram. Dead legs hide behind blind exchanger readings; start there with <link=0xFF667A36>.

Waste Heat Scavenger // Waste heat scavenger is a coil wrapped around someone else's bad efficiency. Useful for thawing valves and warming cells, dangerous when it steals margin from life support. Fit bypass, label the thermal debt, and never make heat recovery a hidden dependency. Battery heater notes continue in <link=0x58BFFA5E>.

Condensate Frost // Condensate frost around a valve is a map of pressure drop and thermal insult. Thin white bloom means inspect. Heavy rim means flow is choking. Frost that grows after shutdown means a leak is still feeding it. Do not lick it, joke about it, or ignore it. Valve freeze procedure is <link=0x1B785540>.

AUP Route Marker // AUP route marker stores grid coordinate and local offset so the world can shift without losing the way home. Paint marks are for eyes; hashes are for machines. If a route crosses a rebase boundary, trust the marker only after the local offset quantizes clean. Map cache behavior is covered in <link=0xB0990C70>.

Sonar No-Range Return // No-range sonar return means bearing exists but distance is contaminated by multipath, absorption, or something moving too wide for the pulse model. Do not call it contact and do not call it safe. Log bearing, reduce speed, and wait for a second channel. Acoustic pinger discipline is <link=0xFC9E0142>.

Manual Compass // Manual compass is sealed, weighted, and dumb enough to survive a software argument. It hates local current, big metal, and crew who forget deviation cards. Use it when the PDA map jitters or the sonar starts selling poetry. For dead-reckoning cleanup, use the board method in <link=0xD69B86D9>.

Dead Reckoning Slate // Dead reckoning slate is a wet panel with heading, time, thrust, and shame. It will not be exact. It will be less wrong than a corrupted route cache. Update every turn, not every panic. If AUP marker and slate disagree, stop moving until <link=0x48A2F614> is reconciled.

PDA Scan Cache // PDA scan cache keeps discovered pages by hash and mask, not by string title. That keeps lookup cheap and prevents the archive from inventing records because a label changed. If the page is missing, show the fallback and log once. Streaming rules are expanded in <link=0xD0520D07>.

Map POI Upload // Map POI upload is a dirty-page job. If the points did not change, do not shove them across the bus to feel productive. Low tier sends compact positions; high tier can afford smoother fade and richer glyphs. The upload still obeys the same cache law as <link=0xB0990C70>.

Acoustic Pinger // Acoustic pinger is a timed lie used carefully. It says where sound survived, not where truth lives. Thorp absorption handles open-water loss; enclosed module echo uses a Sabine RT60 estimate, not mood. Hard walls, silt, and moving hulls can fold a pulse into a false bearing. Use two pings separated by motion; if the return follows the helmet, inspect the suit before the sea. Related no-range warning is <link=0xBAAA654F>.

Depth Palette Note // Depth color saturates early because Beer-Lambert attenuation kills red before the PDA gets poetic. Below that, readability comes from silhouette, fog, emissive biomes, thermal orange, scanner UI, and audio pressure. Do not promise unique blue for every deeper meter. The ocean already spent that palette. Navigation lights should follow <link=0x718EA2F1>.

Signal Timing 11:23 // A clean repeated interval is data until it starts making decisions for you. The 11:23 timing mark is logged as cadence, not intent. Correlate with power spikes, fauna silence, and route lockouts before naming causes. Black Box capture in <link=0xC640B428> keeps the argument from becoming campfire theater.

Blackwater Visibility // Blackwater visibility is not solved by more light. More light can flatten contrast, wake predators, and advertise panic. Use narrow beam, sonar pulse, and panel glow. If particles erase the route, slow down instead of blooming the lamp. Worklamp doctrine starts at <link=0x4E0CE002>.

Scrap Sorter Assay // Scrap sorter assay uses density, magnet response, and conductivity before anyone names a prize. Paint color is not metallurgy. Corporate tags lie after fire, brine, and lawyers. Sort into copper, titanium, ceramic, and junk, then let the fabricator complain with numbers. Copper salvage is tied to <link=0xCC2BA613>.

Titanium Laminate // Titanium laminate is strong until bad prep turns it into expensive wallpaper. Grind bright, wipe salt, clamp flat, then bond under pressure. Do not bridge paint, rust bloom, or old sealant. If the patch needs to carry pressure, run the hull procedure in <link=0xA6EBA6A7> instead of improvising sculpture.

Sealant Pack Handling // Sealant pack stock has a shelf life, temperature band, and a bad attitude after freezing. Warm it in hand heat or waste coil, not open flame. Purge first centimeter because grit collects in the nozzle. If the bead foams, the surface is wet or the pack is dead. Printed gasket use is <link=0xA6292BAA>.

Printed Gasket // Printed gasket is acceptable for low-cycle covers, inspection ports, and the kind of leak that insults boots instead of killing crews. It is not a pressure-door miracle. Print oversize, trim, grease lightly, and torque in star pattern. For real door load, return to <link=0x92C8F4E9>.

Copper Bus Salvage // Copper bus salvage starts with power proof, not enthusiasm. De-energize, discharge, cut lugs, and keep green corrosion out of the good bin. A bright copper strip can still be annealed soft after a heat event. Check bracket movement and fault history using <link=0x977063DA>.

Lens Polishing // Scanner lens polish is not vanity. A scratched lens throws false scatter into range estimates and makes the PDA blame water for human neglect. Use figure-eight strokes, clean slurry, and inspect under narrow light. If sonar and optics disagree after polish, escalate to pinger validation in <link=0xFC9E0142>.

Bearing Rebuild // Bearing rebuild needs clean grease, matched balls, and patience the station no longer stocks. If the race is pitted, do not pretend fresh grease is repair. A bad bearing sings before it seizes, and that song travels through hull plates like gossip. Turbine overpitch damage is logged in <link=0xEC227511>.

Ceramic Fuse // Ceramic fuse is there to die instead of the system. Replacing it with wire is not fieldcraft; it is delayed arson. Match rating, check downstream fault, and save the blown fuse because its fracture pattern tells whether the hit was surge or overload. Ground fault checks start at <link=0xB3618564>.

Microfracture Dye // Microfracture dye makes cracks confess under narrow light. Clean, apply, wait, wipe, inspect. A line that reappears after wiping is a crack; a smear is dirty technique. Use dye before welding, after impact, and whenever a wall starts making polite noises. Habitat stress states begin at <link=0x9164B86F>.

Fabricator Feed Jam // Fabricator feed jam usually means mixed scrap, wet powder, or a crew trying to print hope from trash. Kill heat, reverse feed, clear with brass hook, then run a dry purge. Do not force the ram; bent feed screws turn every future print into evidence. Material sorting begins with <link=0x64358FB7>.

Cold Current Suit // Cold current does not need drama. It takes heat through a simple exponential slide toward ambient. If insulation is damaged, the slide gets steep and fingers get stupid. Log external temperature, internal temperature, and battery heater load before blaming the suit. Heater cost belongs to <link=0x58BFFA5E>.

Thermal Vent Warning // Thermal vent water is not friendly because it is warm. It carries chemistry, flow shear, and sensor lies. Treat orange light as a hazard marker unless a survey says otherwise. Use vent heat for scavenging only through a controlled exchanger. Dead-leg heat traps are explained in <link=0x2E161104>.

Radiation Scrubber // Radiation scrubber is shielding, filter media, and logging discipline. It reduces dose rate; it does not cleanse courage or inventory mistakes. Check cumulative dose, media color, and seal seating before entering a hot room. If the PDA reports comfort while the badge darkens, trust the badge and file under <link=0x962CE0E0>.

Nitrogen Narcosis Checklist // Nitrogen narcosis starts as confidence with bad handwriting. At high pressure, cognition gets noisy before the body admits trouble. Use buddy math, short commands, and instrument cross-checks. If somebody laughs at warning lights, reduce task load and revisit Dalton bookkeeping in <link=0x0EE1BD03>.

Hypoxia Response // Hypoxia response is not a speech contest. Sit the diver down, verify O2 partial pressure, check regulator flow, and stop them from doing clever work. Blue lips are late evidence. Bad decisions arrive first. Use the emergency pocket only after confirming it is not a CO2 trap with <link=0xAD55D9F9>.

CO2 Headache // CO2 headache is the room billing you for bad scrub. Symptoms: heat, pressure behind eyes, anger at simple tasks, and the belief that another minute is fine. Another minute is not fine. Swap media, raise ventilation, and audit the scrubber bed. Start with <link=0xE8DF429A>.

Heat Exchanger Wet // A wet heat exchanger loses efficiency and starts growing failures in layers: corrosion, insulation rot, sensor drift, then a polite fire alarm with no visible fire. Dry it, pressure test it, and check coolant flow under load. If readings stay pretty, suspect a blind spot from <link=0xFF667A36>.

Insulation Pinhole // Insulation pinhole is small until the suit crosses a cold seam. Then heat leaves through that dot like debt through a company account. Mark with dye, patch dry, and retest under cold flow. Do not count on body heat to make up the loss; the heater tax is in <link=0x58BFFA5E>.

Battery Heater Tax // Battery heater tax is the watts paid to keep cells honest in cold water. It reduces available tool time and makes fake full packs reveal themselves under load. Budget heater draw before cutter work or scooter tow. If the cells sag anyway, inspect the bank behavior in <link=0x415A1629>.

Frosted Valve Caution // Frosted valve gets one gentle test, not a wrestling match. Ice can hold a seal shut until torque snaps the stem and hands the room to the sea. Warm the body, tap the bonnet, then move in pulses. If frost returns after closure, hunt the pressure drop using <link=0x6EA5707D>.

Scooter Cavitation // Scooter cavitation is the little motor screaming that it is making vapor instead of thrust. Back off throttle, change angle, and let flow reattach. Pushing harder just buys noise, heat, and a shorter swim home. If towing a vessel, compare propwash silt behavior with <link=0x2589AE1F>.

Submarine Auto-Level // Auto-level is a control assist, not a priest. It trims pitch and roll with ballast and thrust, then waits for the hull to answer. Chasing zero every frame wastes power and makes passengers sick. Use damped corrections, not panic toggles. Manual ballast notes are in <link=0x842C5EB5>.

Ballast Bladder Patch // Ballast bladder patch must flex, seal, and not shed into the pump. Clean rubber, roughen lightly, apply patch, cure under mild pressure, then cycle shallow. A patch that holds at dock can still fold under depth load. Watch auto-level response afterward using <link=0x677D4A12>.

Hull Stress Alarm // Hull stress alarm is a thresholded warning from a simplified fatigue model. It does not know fear, debt, or whether the crew is nearly done. Above critical, stop task stacking and reduce pressure exposure. If alarm and analog needle disagree, believe the uglier reading and inspect <link=0x6CC67A80>.

Docking Collar // Docking collar must align before it seals. If the clamps pull the vessels together from bad angle, the gasket folds and the pressure test becomes theater. Use low thrust, visual marks, and one mechanic with authority to abort. Final seal torque borrows rules from <link=0x92C8F4E9>.

Drone Repair Loop // Repair drone loop is useful until it starts polishing the same wound forever. Give it bounded targets, fixed material budget, and a hard return timer. A drone that cannot explain its repair should not own the repair. If it comes back time-shifted, record with <link=0xC640B428> before reuse.

Propwash Silt // Propwash silt is visibility debt. It sells motion, hides predators, and ruins scan confidence. Low tier can fake it with particles and fog masks; high tier can layer richer local response. The physics truth stays with vehicle control, not every grain. Visibility doctrine continues in <link=0x3E33154E>.

Cabin Pressure Gauge // Cabin pressure gauge is the room's pulse. It must be analog-backed, eye-readable, and checked before anyone opens a door into a new pressure story. Total pressure does not prove breathable mix, but it proves the door will have opinions. Pair with Dalton math from <link=0x0EE1BD03>.

Navigation Light Discipline // Navigation lights show shape and intent, not bravery. Use low-output markers, sector blink codes, and shielded lamps so the water reads your silhouette without turning the vessel into bait. If depth palette is saturated, lights carry readability. Cross-reference <link=0x9EB943C5>.

Emergency Ascent No // Emergency ascent is not a reset button. From depth it trades one failure for decompression injury, hull shock, lost tools, and a report nobody wants to write. Ascend by envelope unless the module is already lost. If stress is critical, count exits and evidence first. Habitat terminal state is <link=0x7E20B34A>.

Black Box 300 Frame // Critical systems keep a 300-frame ring of positions, hashes, flags, and high-level state because 'no idea' is not a diagnostic category. On NaN, crash, or impossible transition, dump the ring before memory goes soft. This is how lies get shorter. NaN quarantine protocol follows in <link=0x38482363>.

NaN Quarantine // NaN is a leak in arithmetic. If a float feeding physics or rendering stops being finite, replace with safe fallback, flag telemetry, and dump context. Do not let one bad division teach the hull to fly. Any dumped record should carry stable tags, usually from the FNV ledger in <link=0x1245A8FA>.

FNV Tag Ledger // FNV tag ledger gives authored text and systems stable numeric handles. Keys are not prose; prose changes and keys stay. If a PDA entry links another record, it links the hash, not a title that localization will bend later. This entry is the reason every page can point at <link=0xB0990C70> without string lookup.

Save Packet Note // Save packet stores divergence, not the whole ocean. Dead doors, cut resources, placed structures, and unlocked records matter. Every pretty particle that can be recomputed from seed stays out. If a text record unlocks, store the bit, not the paragraph. PDA bitmask rules start in <link=0xB0990C70>.

Addressable Cache Ticket // Addressable cache ticket says who loaded a thing, who still owns it, and when it can be released. Fire-and-forget loads are just leaks wearing boots. Text payloads are cheap, but cheap still needs an owner. If the PDA streams pages on demand, it follows <link=0xD0520D07>.

PDA Page Streaming // PDA page streaming reads by hash, fills a fixed char buffer, and refuses to allocate just because the player scrolls fast. Missing key returns a fixed error, logs once, and stays boring. Richer hardware may add glitch overlays; the text path remains dull and safe. Hash behavior is in <link=0x1245A8FA>.

Text Decay Table // Text decay is pre-authored substitution and shader behavior, not live madness prose. Stress can choose a version or corrupt glyphs from a table; it must not allocate a fresh sentence every frame. The Habitat Integrity stress run proves the content side. Start at <link=0x9164B86F>.

Lockout Placard // Lockout placard has three useful fields: what is isolated, why, and who is allowed to kill power again. Anything else is office perfume. If the placard says temporary and the salt line says old, believe the salt. Confirm electrical isolation with the bracket and fault checks in <link=0x977063DA>.

Marauder QA Stamp // Marauder QA stamp is not approval; it is blame with coordinates. Stamp only after the repair survives pressure, power, thermal, and human stupidity checks. Write what was rejected, not just what was done. If the next diver cannot reproduce the decision, the stamp is trash. Link evidence to <link=0xC640B428>.

Final Field Rule // Final field rule: map exit, count air, kill comfort load, trust analog when firmware smiles, and write the failure in words a tired diver can use. The ocean punishes vague nouns. If a log cannot tell the next crew how the machine breaks, it is decoration. Start the chain again at <link=0xC2DCC831>.
